summary: Spine of "Old Plays, Vol. 59" (Mal. 216) pasted onto the front pastedown.  Front flyleaf with contents list for Mal 216.  Note by Malone on front flyleaf: "The only edition. Perhaps this title page and an imperfect recollection of the piece itself was the origin of Pope's ascribing the old K. John printed in 1591, to Shakespeare and Rowley. He remembered I suppose having seen these names coupled somewhere together, and forgot the particular piece. To the old K. John printed by S. Clarke in 1591 no author's name is prefixed. The greatest part of the present play was intended as verse, tho' the printer has, for the sake of saving a sheet or two of paper, exhibited it almost entirely as prose. Shakespeare, I am confident, wrote not a line of it. M."  Below this note, in different ink: "Wm. Rowley wrote for a different theatre. This piece was probably written about the year 1615."

summary: Catalogue description bound in at front. A letter from Henrietta Bartlett to Walter Thomas Wallace is bound in at front, dated 9 Oct 1912: "My dear Mr Wallace - Many thanks for the full particulars as to your Shakespeare collection which is a nice one even if there is only one item in it which comes within my present scope. If you could have only one quarto, I am glad it is an undated 'Julius Caesar' for I have studied that play bibliographically for two years and am sending you under separate cover the results of my research. My opinion as to the arrangement of editions was approved by Messrs. W. A. White, Beverly Chew and L.S. Livingston here as well as Mr. Pollard and Mr. H. B. Wheatley in England although we are none of us sure as to 'Quarto 5'. [inserted in pencil] ^the one of 60pp. considerably later than mine^  All I know is that none of them could have been printed before 1682 and I think '5' comes after the 1684 one. I am naturally very anxious to see your copy and make a careful examination for the the Census as well as for my own satisfaction. If you would be so very kind as to bring it over to town with you and then let me come down to your office and examine it, I should be much grateful. If you would prefer to bring it up here, I will borrow Mr. White's copies when I go over there on Tuesday next and we can make it absolutely certain as to which edition it belonged to. If it's not too much trouble and you would call me up on the phone (5360 Spring) any morning this week before 12 o'clock, I could arrange about Mr. White's books as it's so much better to make the physical comparison. I shall be out Monday and Tuesday of next week but any time after that will suit me and I will gladly go to you if that suits you better. New copies of 'Julius Caesar' are like glittering El Dorados to me now. Hoping you will be interested too, I am truly yours, Henrietta C. Bartlett."

title: The Taming of a/the Shrew
summary: Title page only, with portrait in state 1. Trimmed within platemark, not affecting text. Also known as the "Halliwell-Phillipps Unique Proof" (though now known not to be unique) and the "Lilly Proof." Removed from Halliwell-Phillipps volume labeled "The proof engraving of Droeshout’s portrait of Shakespeare, 1623." Encapsulated with a note in Halliwell-Phillipps’ hand that reads: "This engraving belonged to an imperfect copy of the First Folio that was purchased by Lilly at a sale at Sotheby’s on 11 May, 1863, lot 110, and I bought the engraving itself of Lilly exactly a year afterwards, 11 May, 1864, for one hundred guineas." That copy of the First Folio (West 39) is now owned by the Royal Shakspeare Theatre and kept by the Shakespeare Birthplace Trust at the Shakespeare Centre Library. Only four impressions of state 1 are known: one at the British Library (c.39.k.15), one at the Bodleian (Arch. G.c.8) and two at the Folger (ART Box D783 no.1 and STC 22273 Fo.1 no.02, title page).

summary: This copy was exhibited by Christie's, 2-26 May 2023, and is therefore verified. It is currently owned privately. See https://www.christies.com/en/events/shakespeare-first-folio-exhibition/about . In this copy as it currently stands, the Histories precede the Comedies. Since "The missing plays include the four comedies which ordinarily appear at the beginning [Tem, TGV, MWW, MM] and Cym., which ordinarily comes at the end," Hook surmises that "the volume, originally bound ... in the normal order, was heavily damaged both at the front and back, and when it was rebound, the order of the plays was changed" (335). summary: In this copy the crossbar of the "f" in "fold" in the imprint has begun to break off. Leaf 3d4 lined and reattached. [Superscript pi]A1 remargined. Title leaf ([superscript pi]A2) from what W.B. Todd describes as the first issue, variant 1b, printed in 1632. Based on description in the Barton Collection catalog, this leaf was inserted to replace the missing, original title page. [Superscript pi]A5, containing both the Milton epitaph and an anonymous effigy, wanting and replaced in facsimile that displays what both Todd and R.M. Smith refer to as the “effigies B” variant. Extra, but authentic “effigies” leaf (Todd: "effigies C"), here autographed by Thomas Davies, also inserted. Because the issues and variants of the Second Folio are differentiated via their front matter -- multiple leaves of which are, in this copy, reinserted, possibly from a different copy or group of copies -- the entirety of G.174.3 cannot be conclusively ascribed to any single issue.

summary: From dealer catalogue: "a few small damp stains to margins, 5 tiny holes to the first page of The Comedy of Errors (with slight loss of 3 letters of text), a couple of short closed marginal tears, a little slight soiling and browning .... Lacking the initial leaf, To the Reader, but with all other leaves present and mostly intact. The first 17 and last 19 leaves have been neatly repaired (not recently), with some loss of the ruled border and/or varying degrees of minor text loss to 25 of those leaves, usually only a few words or less to the last few lines. The title and colophon pages have both been laid down, and there is some loss of the imprint at the foot of the title page, including almost all of the date. (The text that remains is: London, Printed by Tho. Cotes, for William Aspley, and are [...] of the Parrat in Pauls Church-yard. 1...). The inner margin of the final leaf has loss of much of the ruled border, portions of each of the last 17 lines of text (usually only a couple of words per line), and the beginning of the two-line colophon: the first word of line one, and part of the initial 'R' from the first word of line two. The five publisher's names and, most importantly, the 1632 date are all intact. The title page portrait of Shakespeare by Martin Droeshout is in the third state, with the tiny difference in the highlighting of the eyes and the extra strand of hair to the right side of the coiffure. The letter 'M' is missing from the artist's name, but the portrait is complete and a fine impression."

The variance of the present state of this copy from earlier descriptions of it (Edward Hartley sale catalogue, Sotheby’s, Mar. 25, 1925, and notes penciled on the rear pastedown) and the presence of many binder’s stubs, passim, indicate extensive doctoring of this copy.  The precise extent of the alterations cannot be determined, but evidently supplied from another copy or copies are H3, H4, s5, 3c5, and 3c6.  Full documentation on file.  Accompanied by related correspondence, manuscript notes, newspaper clippings, and a port. of "Mrs. Garrick" from Lady’s Magazine (1831), as accumulated by Hartley (perhaps some by Beltz)--housed with the documentation of this copy. Tipped in (ibid.) is Hartley’s manuscript "Collation of 2nd Folio ..." based on W.T. Lowndes, Bibliographer’s manual, rev. H.G. Bohn (1869), 2256-57.

title: Comedies, Histories, and Tragedies: F1
summary: Folger copy 42 is nominally of STC 22274e.3  However, the issue cannot be definitively determined.  This copy contains πA(πA2) (cancellans title leaf) proper to the second issue, but in place of its conjugate, πA(πA5) (cancellans "Effigies" leaf) proper to the second issue, this copy contains πA5 (cancellandum "Effigies" leaf) proper to the first issue (in state Ib); either (or both) of these leaves could be supplied from another copy.  The title leaf present is cut down, lacking the last line of the imprint, and is mounted, and the "Effigies" leaf present is extended. Wants πA1,3,4.  Present as prelim. leaves are, in the order bound: facsim. of 1st Folio leaf πA5; πA(πA2) (cancellans title leaf proper to the second issue; condition as recorded above); facsim. of 1st Folio πA6; πA5 (cancellandum "Effigies" leaf proper to the first issue; condition as recorded above); πA6; facsim. of 1st Folio πA5+2; *1 (mutilated--the headpiece excised--and patched); and *2-4. Port. (on title page) in state 3. Elsewhere this copy wants leaves or contains leaves demonstrably supplied from other copies or contains leaves questionable by reason of their idiosyncratic size or marks of soil: H3, genuine; N1.6, perhaps supplied; R6, likely supplied; 2B4, likely supplied; 2B5, wanting (supplied is the leaf bearing the corresponding text in the 3rd Folio--2B5); b1-5, perhaps supplied; d1,4,6, probably genuine; u1-4, perhaps supplied; u5-y6 (Hen. VIII entire), wanting (supplied are the leaves bearing some of the corresponding text in the 1st Folio--t6, v1,6, and x1-4, with v6 and x1-3 mutilated, affecting text); 2h2-5, perhaps supplied; and 2q3.4, perhaps supplied.  Of Cymb.: 3b6, supplied; 3c1, wanting; 3c2-5, perhaps supplied; 3c6, supplied; and 3d1-4 (including the colophon), wanting. Imperfections affect text on T2, slightly on F3, r1, and 2b4, and very slightly on I3, Q1, b4, p1, 2m1, and 2t4.

title: Comedies, Histories, and Tragedies: F1
summary: In Folger copy 15, πA1 is wanting; supplied in facsim.  Leaf πA2 (title leaf) is mutilated toward the lower outer corner, affecting the port. and imprint on the title page  The leaf is patched, with the affected part of the t.p. touched up with pen and ink or supplied in facsim.  Although the imprint on the t.p. is affected, the t.p. otherwise exhibits enough of the distinctive points of issue 3 to demonstrate that it is of that issue.  The extreme upper outer corner of πA2 (title leaf) also is patched.  Most (if not all) leaves of gatherings πA and * and of gatherings 3b, 3c, and 3d (Cymb.) are guarded. Port. (on title page) in state 3. When sold at Sotheby’s, Feb. 23, 1925, as lot 337 (in a condition "not subject to return"), this copy, according to the descripton in the sale catalog, wanted (aside from πA1, now supplied in facsim.) *2,3 and L3,4, which leaves are now supplied from another copy.  Discolored and pressed the same as L3,4 are E6, R4, y3,4,5, 2c4, 2y3-2z2, 3b1-6, 3c3-3d4, so these leaves also are likely suplied from another copy. title: Comedies, Histories, and Tragedies: F1
summary: Folger copy 38 is nominally of STC 22274e.5. However, the issue cannot be definitively determined.  This copy contains πA(πA2) (cancellans title leaf), the recto of which (title page) reads consistently as of the third issue, but in place of its conjugate, πA(πA5) (cancellans "Effigies" leaf) proper to the third issue, this copy contains πA5 (cancellandum "Effigies" leaf) proper to the first issue (in state Ib); either (or both) of these leaves could be supplied from another copy. On πA(πA2) recto (title page), the first line of the title statement and the three lines of the imprint are touched up or supplied in pen-and-ink facsim.  In the imprint, the swash "R" of "Robert", recorded by Giles E. Dawson, TLS, Feb. 1, 1947, p. 65, is unquestionably supplied in manuscript and accordingly is not a press variant. Port. (on title page) in state 3. Leaves πA2-*1 have margins patched very unobtrusively and probably have adjacent text touched up with pen and ink. Leaves 3c3-5 are mutilated in the outer margin, affecting the catchword on 3c4 recto and some rules.  Wanting 3d4 (including the colophon); supplied in manuscript facsim. Leaf e6 (short and narrow and watermarked redundantly with e1) is supplied from another copy.  Either leaf f1 or f6 (watermarked redundantly) is supplied from another copy; probably f1 (touched up with pen and ink on the recto).  Leaf 2y6 (short, guarded) is probably supplied from another copy. Imperfections affect text very slightly on A3, E4, u6, and 2h5.

title: Comedies, Histories, and Tragedies: F1
summary: Title page in facsimile; Contains a letter from F. G. Kenyon (Dept of manuscripts, British Museum) to Dr Leeper, discussing this edition of Shakespeare (June 9th 1904): 'Dear Sir, Your Shakespeare arrived two days ago considerably later than your letter on the subject. One of my colleagues in the department of Printed Books has examined it carefully, and he reports that it is as you have always supposed, a copy of the Second Folio, with the exception of the last leaf, which is from the Third Folio. You will notice that the top outer corner of this leaf has been torn off, do doubt in order to conceal the fact that the pagination did not correspond with that of the rest of the volume. About half of the preliminary matter is wanting, the most important leaves being among those which have disappeared. Of course this would affect the pecunary value of the book very considerably, and my colleague remarks that the £50 for which the book was insured is probably quite as much as it it worth". I mention this, not because I suppose you would wish to sell the volume, or because it real value as evidence for the text of Shakespeare is in any way affected, but merely because the deatil may be of interest to you. I am returning the book separately as an insured parcel. Yours sincerely, F.S. Kenyon)'

summary: Fragment: As You Like It only. A note found inside the copy reads: ""This is one of the important monuments of English literature, as it is an interesting example of the book art of its period. Roman type, with woodcut initials followed after the decorative Black Letter of previous years. Margins were set off in black lines as later printers were to imitate. It was upon an edition of the Second Folio that the handwriting of Ben Johnson and George II were found, and Milton referred to this edition in his "Iconoclasters." This is but one section of the larger work."

Lacking all leaves through M6 (prelims., Temp., Two Gent., Merry Wives, M. for M., Errors, Much Ado, and LLL). Also wants N2-4, 2N2, 3L1, 3P5,6, 4C1-4E4 (Cymb.), and b1 through end (the end of Pericles and the rest of the additional plays entire). Leaves a1-6 (beginning of Pericles) are misbound at the front of the book. Leaves N1,5, R1, and a1 are mutilated and (except R1) patched, affecting text (only slightly on R1). Other imperfections affect text slightly on 2Y1 and very slightly on S3, Y1, 2D6, and 2L1. Variant states and printings, as recorded by James G. McManaway, "New discoveries in the Third Folio," PBSA, v. 70, (1976), 469-80, and other such variations, are identified in file.

title: Comedies, Histories, and Tragedies: F2
summary: Includes: 1664 title leaf, and the additional plays. The 1664 title leaf is patched at the inner edge and tail, affecting letterpress of title page, with the affected text supplied in manuscript facsim. or touched up with pen and ink.  The t.p. is red-ruled and the leaf mounted. Wants the associated "verses"; supplied is the corresponding leaf in the 4th Folio, [pi]1--the "verses" on the verso, with the port. above them in state 4.  The leaf is remargined in the upper and outer margins, and the page of "verses is red-ruled. Leaf πA3 is remargined (except at the tail), affecting letterpress on the verso, with the affected text supplied in manuscript facsim. Supplied from another copy are A1 or A6, perhaps 2M6, 2N1 (probably) or 2N6, 2X2 or 2X5, and [par.]G6.  Leaf [par.]G6 is patched, affecting text, with the affected text supplied in manuscript facsim. Imperfections affect text on T1, slightly on 2H5 and 2Q4, and very slightly on 12 other leaves (list on file). Variant states and printings, as recorded by James G. McManaway, "New discoveries in the Third Folio," PBSA, v. 70, (1976), 469-80, and other such variations, are identified in file.

title: Comedies, Histories, and Tragedies: F2

title: Comedies, Histories, and Tragedies: F3
summary: This copy includes the title page with three publishers in the imprint (Wing S2915). This copy was not known to Greg, Dawson, or Hansen and Rasmussen. From auction catalogue: "In this copy some sheets have been reprinted at an early date--all identifiable by the absence of rules at the sides and foot of the text--as Greg records occurred in some cases: "In the...second section a number of the sheets appear to have been printed short, or else some accident happened to the stock. When, as the supply became depleted, the discrepancy was discovered, the deficient sheets were reprinted. These reprints are readily distinguished from the originals by the absence of rules at the sides and foot of the text. So far six copies have been identified (four Folger, two New York) containing between them seventeen reprinted sheets..." (W.W. Greg, A Bibliography of the English Printed Drama to the Restoration. Vol. III., pp.1120-21). In the present copy nine of these seventeen sheets appear to be reprints: 2B3.4, 2I2.5, 2I3.4, 2M1.6, 2N1.6, 2N2.5, 2O3.4, *3B2.5, *3C2.5 and *3C3.4."

Paton treats the Plutarch (1612), specifically the copy the title page of which is pictured in the photoreproduction (supposedly Shakespeare’s own, then in the Greenock Library) in his Introduction to his edition of Cor. W. H. Hutton, and a review of a performance in Edinburgh of "Mr. Forbes Robertson in the ’Sacrament of Judas’".-- "Merry Wives of Windsor.  Act 1. Scene 1. . . . Painted by R. Smirke.  Engraved by M. Haughton.  Pub. June 4, 1801, by J. & J. Boydell at the Shakespeare Gallery. ...", stipple engraving.--ephemera relating to Isabella Dallas Glyn.
